title: Deployment rehearsal playbook & failure catalog (Sept 2026) [draft]
content:
OVERVIEW
This doc is a hands-on rehearsal playbook for the September 2026 production deployment window. Primary goal: run at least two end-to-end dry runs that exercise the full cutover path (routing, model variant fallback, KV cache warm, autoscale on load) and capture observed failure modes in a compact catalog so we can harden runbooks and rollback criteria.

GOALS
- Validate the orchestration handoff between release-engineering, serving-runtime, and platform-engineering.
- Exercise graceful degradation (model fallback to quantized variant).
- Verify telemetry, alerts, and release-notes publishing pipeline.
- Produce a short, actionable failure catalog with triage notes.

SCOPE
- Includes hosted API route changes, config flips for cache TTL, and model variant promotion.
- Excludes any database schema migrations and org-level IAM updates.

REHEARSAL SCHEDULE (slots)
- Slot A: 2026-09-20 02:00-03:30 UTC (primary dry-run, low-traffic) Owner: Marco Alvarez
- Slot B: 2026-09-22 18:00-19:30 UTC (blue/green simulation under synthetic load) Owner: Dana Park
- Postmortem & fixes: 2026-09-24 15:00-16:00 UTC Owner: Aisha Kumar

ROLES & CONTACTS
- Release lead: Aisha Kumar (pager: aisha@redwood, slack: @aisha)
- Orchestration + traffic: Marco Alvarez
- Runtime & model team: Dana Park
- SRE on-call: Riley O'Neill
- Observability: telemetry-team (shared on-call list)

PRE-RUN CHECKLIST (to be completed 24-48h before slot)
- [ ] Create ephemeral release tag and document commit SHAs (release-engineering checklist).
- [ ] Verify canary traffic route and preconfigured canary percentage.
- [ ] Populate synthetic traffic job and smoke test payloads.
- [ ] Confirm alerting thresholds and notification channels.
- [ ] Confirm rollback runbook is published in Confluence and linked in incident channel.

RUN SEQUENCE (high level)
1) Announce start in #releases and set channel to read-only for non-ops.
2) Snapshot config and take small telemetry baseline (latency p90/p99, error rates, token cost).
3) Deploy control-plane changes to staging then to canary nodes.
4) Warm KV cache by replaying representative prompts (see smoke tests).
5) Shift 5% traffic to canary variant, run 15-minute smoke window.
6) If smoke looks good, progress to 30% then 60% with stabilizing delays.
7) If automated health gates pass, promote to full routing, observe for 30m.
8) If any gate fails, follow rollback decision matrix below.

SMOKE TEST MATRIX (minimal)
- Auth / token validation: 3 calls, expected 200
- Short completions: 10 requests, p95 < 120ms
- Long-form generation: 5 requests, stream integrity + no truncation
- Function/tool-calling path: 5 requests, call executed and returned structured payload
- Embeddings baseline: 3 batch requests, cosine similarity sanity check
- KV cache hitrate: baseline > 60% after warmup
- Billing/usage metric sanity: token counts within 10% of synthetic job expected

OBSERVED FAILURE CATALOG (initial entries)
1) Failure id: F-2026-09-01-A - Model variant memory pressure
   - Reproduction: ramped 1000 concurrent long-form streams on a 24G GPU variant.
   - Observed: OOM on worker, process restart, requests returned 503 for ~45s.
   - Immediate mitigation: throttle to lower concurrency, abort queued streams; promote to fallback quantized variant.
   - Long-term: add aggressive auto-shed/queue limit and per-tenant concurrency caps.

2) Failure id: F-2026-09-02-B - KV cache inconsistency after quick rollback
   - Reproduction: performed rapid promote->rollback within 60s window.
   - Observed: stale KV pointers led to incorrect completions for 3% of requests.
   - Mitigation: flush prefix cache on rollback and mark TTLs as zero for 2m.
   - Action: add forced cache-invalidate hook to rollback step.

3) Failure id: F-2026-09-08-C - Telemetry missing sample points during surge
   - Reproduction: synthetic load with burst mode triggered metrics aggregation lag.
   - Observed: alerting did not trigger for 2m because aggregator backlog grew.
   - Mitigation: bypass heavy aggregation path for critical SLO metrics; fallback to raw event stream sampling.

ROLLBACK DECISION MATRIX (quick guide)
- Blocker (immediate rollback): request error rate > 5% for 5 min OR p99 latency > 2s AND user-facing feature failures.
- High (consider rollback unless mitigation within 10 min): model OOMs, sustained GC spikes, or persistent partial correctness failures.
- Medium (mitigate in place then evaluate): temporary increased cost, transient latency spikes under 3 min.
- If rollback performed: run cache invalidation, revert traffic routing, and run verification smoke tests before reattempt.

COMMUNICATION PLAN
- Pre-run: announce planned windows 48h/24h and pin quick instructions.
- During run: use #releases thread with structured updates (Start, Gate1, Gate2, Promote, Finish).
- Incident: open incident doc with timeline and link to run logs; assign triage owner.
- Post-run: publish one-paragraph summary to product-announce channel and attach release notes draft.

POST-RUN ARTIFACTS (what to collect)
- Run log (annotated timeline) exported from orchestration tool.
- Snapshot of metrics (p50/p95/p99, error rates) stored in artifact bucket.
- Synthetic payload responses for failed tests (for debugging).
- Updated failure-catalog entries and follow-up JIRA tickets.

DRAFT RELEASE NOTES (short form to iterate after successful run)
- Feature: Promote model v2.3.1 to production for reduced token cost and improved context handling.
- Ops: Cache TTL tuning to improve cold-starts and lower per-token latency.
- Known issues: Intermittent 503 observed under extreme long-form concurrent streaming; automatic fallback to quantized variant is enabled.

RUN LOG EXCERPT (example entries)
- 2026-09-20T02:03Z - Start slot A. Baseline p99 540ms.
- 2026-09-20T02:12Z - Traffic 5% -> canary. Smoke auth failed once (token refresh edge-case).
- 2026-09-20T02:18Z - Mitigation: reissued token cache flush, smoke resumed.
- 2026-09-20T02:40Z - Observed KV cache hitrate 45% (below target) -> ran warmup batch.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs
- Need decision: should rollback flush only prefix or entire cache for safety? (Marco to propose by 2026-09-16).
- Add an automated test that simulates quick promote->rollback sequences (owner: Dana).
- Confirm cost alert thresholds won't spam PagerDuty during synthetic load (SRE to tune).

APPENDIX: QUICK TEMPLATES
- Incident opener template: title, start time, short summary, affected routes, immediate mitigation, next steps.
- Rollback command: orchestration-cli rollback --release <tag> --invalidate-cache-prefix <prefix> --notify-channel #releases

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep this doc intentionally lean; we want the failures to be actionable and reproducible. Capture logs in a shared artifact bucket at path: gs://release-rehearsals/2026-09-slotA/
- After postmortem, convert high-confidence mitigations into small RFCs or PRs.

END OF DRAFT
